title: The 10 Best Cordless Hammer Drills
subtitle: Battery-powered 1/2-inch hammer drills for wood, metal and masonry, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A cordless hammer drill is a drill/driver with a hammer mode for brick, block and concrete anchor holes. Most of the best sellers are sold as bare tools for people who already own the batteries, so check whether a pick is a kit before you buy. We ranked 10 best-sellers on rating, review volume and features (brushless motor, battery included, a two-speed gearbox and an LED). They run from about $63 for a complete kit to $207 for DEWALT's flagship bare tool.

avoid.name: GoYwato 1239In-lbs 21V Brushless Cordless Power Hammer Drill Set with Case
avoid.flag: "21V" drill that runs on Makita 18V packs; capacity claims that don't fit a 1/2 in chuck
avoid.verdict: A no-name kit whose headline numbers don't add up. The Dong Cheng kit costs the same, comes with two batteries, and is rated 4.6.
reasons: It's sold as a 21V drill, but the listing's own fine print says it runs on Makita 18V batteries. "21V" is the peak voltage of an 18V pack, a marketing number, not a more powerful tool.
It claims 1,239 in-lb of torque, more than the brushless Makita XPH16Z (970 in-lb) and close to the Milwaukee M18 FUEL (1,400 in-lb), with no brand or test behind the figure.
The spec table lists a 25 mm metal drilling capacity and a 10 cm wood capacity on a drill with a 13 mm (1/2 in) chuck.
It's a third-party body on another brand's battery, so Makita doesn't warrant it.

buyers_guide.q: Do I need a hammer drill or a regular drill?
buyers_guide.a: A hammer drill does everything a drill/driver does, plus a hammer mode for brick, block and the odd concrete anchor hole. If you ever hang things on masonry, it's worth the small price difference. For lots of concrete, look at a rotary hammer instead.

If you already own batteries for a platform, buy the bare tool and save the cost of a battery and charger. If you don't, a kit is cheaper than buying the pieces separately, and the platform you choose decides which tools you'll buy later.

Brushless motors run cooler, get more work from each charge and last longer, because there are no carbon brushes to wear out. For occasional home use a brushed drill is fine; for regular masonry work, brushless is worth it.

buyers_guide.q: What do torque and BPM mean?
buyers_guide.a: Torque (in-lb or UWO) is twisting force, which matters for big bits and long screws. BPM is blows per minute in hammer mode, which matters for how fast it drills masonry. Brands measure torque differently, so compare within a brand rather than across them.

buyers_guide.q: Can a cordless hammer drill handle concrete?
buyers_guide.a: It can drill anchor holes up to about 1/2 inch in concrete, slowly. If you're drilling more than a few holes, or larger ones, a rotary hammer with SDS-Plus bits will be much faster and easier on your wrist.
